about: The outside services the Social Media Factory can use, for a business owner who has never set up an account like this (spec smf-spec-onboarding-v2.md rev 11, 'Outside services and keys'). The one place prices live: SERVICES.md, the setup checklist, GUIDE.md and the setup skill's walkthroughs all read from here. Every price has the date it was checked and its source; a price older than stale_after_days is shown as 'last checked, see the link' instead of a bare number. spending says how money can run away: subscription (charges on a date whatever you use), plan (a free plan that is never charged; its paid plans are monthly subscriptions), credit (prepaid, stops when it runs out, may run slightly over), free (no money).
always: Keys go in your keys file, never in the chat, an email or a screenshot. Claude opens the file; you paste the key in yourself.
If a key ever lands somewhere it shouldn't (a chat, an email, a screenshot, a recording): make a new key, delete the old one, and put the new one in your keys file.
Screens on these websites change. If what you see doesn't match a step, take a screenshot with nothing private showing (no keys, passwords, codes or customer details) and ask Claude.

services.name: Claude
services.for: running the Social Media Factory at all: you talk, it does the work on your computer
services.cost: Claude Pro, about $20 a month before tax. The free plan can't run the Social Media Factory.
services.limit: It's a subscription: it renews monthly whatever you use. Cancel any time in your Claude settings.
steps: Go to claude.ai and create an account with an email you'll keep. You'll get a code by email to confirm it.
Choose the Pro plan and pay by card. You'll see a confirmation that you're on Pro.
Download the Claude desktop app from claude.ai/download, install it and sign in.
Open the Code tab. That's the part that works with folders on your computer; the Social Media Factory runs there.
services.remove: To stop paying: Claude settings, then Billing, then cancel. Your Social Media Factory folder stays on your computer.

services.name: Metricool
services.for: scheduling posts and videos to your accounts, and reading how they did
services.needed_for: scheduling, one short a day, the TikTok test-and-promote loop, and checking results
services.cost: The Advanced plan or higher: about $53 a month paid yearly ($636 a year) or $67 paid monthly, before tax. The cheaper plans can't connect to the Social Media Factory.
services.limit: It's a subscription: it charges on the renewal date whether you post twice or two hundred times. Start monthly, the lower-risk choice, and set a calendar reminder a few days before it renews.
before: Instagram: a Business or Creator account (in the Instagram app: Settings, then Account type and tools). Linking it to your Facebook Page gives Metricool fuller features.
Facebook: you're an admin of the business's Page, not only of your personal profile.
LinkedIn: for a company page, you're one of its admins. A personal profile works too.
TikTok: your account name, or none yet.
YouTube: which Google account owns the channel. It's often not the one you use every day.
Your phone nearby for security codes, and two-step login turned on for each account.
steps: Check your social accounts are ready (the list above), so you don't pay before they can connect.
Go to metricool.com and sign up with an email your business controls. Turn on two-step login.
Choose the Advanced plan and pay by card. Monthly billing is the lower-risk start.
Create a brand in Metricool for your business: one Metricool brand for each brand in your Social Media Factory.
Connect each social account inside that brand. You log in to each platform yourself; your passwords never go to Claude or the Social Media Factory.
Find your key: in Metricool, Account settings, then API. Copy the token, and the user id shown on the same page.
services.remove: In Metricool: Account settings, then API. Make a new token and the old one stops working. To stop paying, cancel in Billing.

services.short: free plan to start, then fractions of a cent per result
services.name: Apify
services.for: research: what's working on YouTube, Instagram and TikTok, and what people ask on Reddit and X
services.cost: A free plan with $5 of credit every month, no card needed. The credit doesn't carry over. Every research run shows its estimated cost before it starts.
services.limit: On the free plan, research simply stops when the month's $5 is used up, and you're never charged. Paid plans are monthly subscriptions: they renew whatever you use. On a paid plan, also set a monthly usage limit in Settings, then Billing, so usage can't go past it.
steps: Go to apify.com and sign up. No card is needed for the free plan.
Find your key: in the Apify console, Settings, then API and Integrations. Copy the personal API token.
services.remove: In the Apify console: Settings, then API and Integrations. Delete the token, or make a new one.

services.short: about 22 cents per hour of audio
services.name: ElevenLabs
services.for: turning speech into exact words, and telling speakers apart
services.needed_for: answering the onboarding page by voice, and clips from your recordings
services.cost: About 22 cents per hour of audio. The free plan includes about 30 minutes of transcription a month, enough to answer the onboarding page by voice. For clips and regular business use, choose the cheapest paid plan (about $6 a month when checked): the free plan may not include commercial use.
services.limit: The free plan is never charged: when its credit runs out, transcription stops until next month. Paid plans are monthly subscriptions that renew whatever you use; leave extra usage (usage-based billing) turned off so nothing is charged beyond the plan.
steps: Go to elevenlabs.io and sign up. Start on the free plan; you can move up later.
Leave extra usage (usage-based billing) off, so you can't be charged past your plan.
Find your key: your profile, then API keys, then Create. If it asks which permissions to give, allow speech to text. Copy the key.
services.remove: In ElevenLabs: your profile, then API keys. Delete the key.

services.short: a separate developer account; roughly 1 to 20 cents per picture
services.name: OpenAI (AI-made pictures)
services.for: AI-made pictures, only when you ask for one. Carousels and cards don't need it
services.cost: An estimate of roughly 1 to 20 cents a picture, by size and quality, shown before each one. It's a separate OpenAI developer account with its own billing, not a ChatGPT subscription.
services.limit: Add prepaid credit (for example $5) with automatic top-up turned off. When it runs out, pictures stop, though OpenAI may let it run slightly over first. A project budget and email alert only warn you; they don't stop spending.
services.key_note: There's no free way to check this key, so “check my setup” shows it as unverified. That's expected.
steps: Go to platform.openai.com and sign up. This is separate from ChatGPT, even if you already have ChatGPT.
In Billing, add a small prepaid credit and turn automatic top-up off.
Find your key: API keys, then Create new secret key. Copy it straight away; it's only shown once.
services.remove: In the OpenAI platform: API keys. Revoke the key.
